rows.text: No. 36/2005 Monetary Policy Committee's Ms. Atchana Waiquamdee, Assistant Thailand, announced that the Monetary Policy economic developments and trends in order to main issues discussed were as follows:
During the first ten months of 2005, particularly in the third quarter where GDP grew the agricultural sector on the supply side, and on the demand side.
Nevertheless, the expansion consumption and investment, has shown some signs of moderating.
The current account has turned around from a large deficit in the first half of the year to a surplus from July onwards.
Headline inflation decelerated from 6.2 per cent in October to 5.9 per cent in November, while core inflation was stable at 2.4 per cent.
The MPC perceived that the Thai economy still has a momentum for continued expansion.
Meanwhile, the risk to inflation, though having moderated, remains and the real interest rates are still negative.
Against that background, the MPC judged that the policy interest rate should stay on an upward path, but the need to adjust the policy rate at a fast pace has diminished.
The MPC therefore decided to raise the 14-day repurchase rate by 25 basis points from 3.75 to 4.00 per cent per annum, effective immediately.
